title: LA SB347: Provides for the crime of "unlawful deepfake" to be added to the definition of power-based violence under the Campus Accountability and Safety Act. (gov sig)

obligations: Not later than the beginning of the fall semester of 2026, the administration of each institution, in consultation with campus or local law enforcement agencies, shall develop and distribute, not less than four times per academic year through in-person or online delivery or both, information to students regarding power based violence, campus safety, and internet and cell phone safety and online content that is a potential threat to school safety (R.S. 17:3399.16(A)).

The information shall include instruction on how to identify and the identification, prevention, dangers, and prohibition of power based violence and how to detect potential threats to school safety exhibited online, including on any social media platform (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(1)).

The information shall include how to report incidents of power based violence, crimes on campus, violations of the student code of conduct, and possible threats to campus safety (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(2)).
The information shall include where to find reports regarding campus safety (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(3)).
The information required in this Subsection shall be updated in consultation with campus or local law enforcement (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(4)).
The information shall be distributed as part of new student orientation and shall be posted on an easily accessible page of each institution's website (R.S. 17:3399.16(C)(1)).
If the student receiving the information is a minor, the information shall also be provided to his parent or legal guardian (R.S. 17:3399.16(C)(2)).
prohibitions: This Act does not itself create a new prohibition. It incorporates conduct prohibited by R.S. 14:73.13 or 73.14 involving media generated by artificial intelligence or deepfake media depicting sexual imagery into the definition of power based violence (R.S. 17:3399.12(5)(b)).

What it does

This Act amends the Campus Accountability and Safety Act to include conduct prohibited by R.S. 14:73.13 or 73.14 involving media generated by artificial intelligence or deepfake media depicting sexual imagery within the definition of power based violence. It also updates the deadline for institutions to develop and distribute safety information from fall 2022 to fall 2026 and revises the required content and distribution methods for that information.

Who it applies to

  • The administration of each institution subject to the Campus Accountability and Safety Act (R.S. 17:3399.16(A))

Effective date

Upon signature by the governor or, if not signed by the governor, upon expiration of the time for bills to become law without signature by the governor, as provided by Article III, Section 18 of the Constitution of Louisiana. If vetoed by the governor and subsequently approved by the legislature, on the day following such approval (Section 2).

Key definitions

  • Power-based violence means any form of interpersonal violence conduct intended to control, coerce, harm, exploit or intimidate another person on the basis of sex through the assertion of power or authority over the person and which shall include dating violence, conduct prohibited by R.S. 14:73.13 or 73.14 involving media generated by artificial intelligence or deepfake media depicting sexual imagery, domestic abuse and family violence, nonconsensual observation of another person's sexuality, sexual assault, sexual exploitation, sexual harassment, stalking and cyberstalking, unlawful communications, and unwelcome sexual or sex or gender based conduct that is objectively offensive, has a discriminatory intent, and lacks a bona fide academic purpose (R.S. 17:3399.12(5)).
  • Sexual exploitation means an act attempted or committed by a person for sexual gratification, financial gain, or other advancement through the abuse of another person's sexuality including prostituting another person (R.S. 17:3399.12(5)(f)).
  • Sexual harassment means unwelcome sexual advances, requests for sexual favors, and other verbal, physical, or inappropriate conduct of a sexual nature when the conduct explicitly or implicitly affects an individual's employment or education, unreasonably interferes with an individual's work or educational performance, or creates an intimidating, hostile, or offensive work or educational environment and has no legitimate relationship to the subject matter of a course or academic research (R.S. 17:3399.12(5)(g)).

Obligations

  • Not later than the beginning of the fall semester of 2026, the administration of each institution, in consultation with campus or local law enforcement agencies, shall develop and distribute, not less than four times per academic year through in-person or online delivery or both, information to students regarding power based violence, campus safety, and internet and cell phone safety and online content that is a potential threat to school safety (R.S. 17:3399.16(A)).
  • The information shall include instruction on how to identify and the identification, prevention, dangers, and prohibition of power based violence and how to detect potential threats to school safety exhibited online, including on any social media platform (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(1)).
  • The information shall include how to report incidents of power based violence, crimes on campus, violations of the student code of conduct, and possible threats to campus safety (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(2)).
  • The information shall include where to find reports regarding campus safety (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(3)).
  • The information required in this Subsection shall be updated in consultation with campus or local law enforcement (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(4)).
  • The information shall be distributed as part of new student orientation and shall be posted on an easily accessible page of each institution's website (R.S. 17:3399.16(C)(1)).
  • If the student receiving the information is a minor, the information shall also be provided to his parent or legal guardian (R.S. 17:3399.16(C)(2)).

Prohibitions

  • This Act does not itself create a new prohibition. It incorporates conduct prohibited by R.S. 14:73.13 or 73.14 involving media generated by artificial intelligence or deepfake media depicting sexual imagery into the definition of power based violence (R.S. 17:3399.12(5)(b)).

Penalties and enforcement

The Act does not state penalties, enforcement authority, or a private right of action (R.S. 17:3399.12 and 3399.16).

How it affects AI deployment

  • An institution deploying AI must include in its safety education information instruction on identifying, preventing, dangers, and prohibition of power based violence, which now includes conduct prohibited by R.S. 14:73.13 or 73.14 involving AI or deepfake sexual imagery (R.S. 17:3399.12(5)(b), 3399.16(B)(1)).
  • An institution must update its safety information in consultation with campus or local law enforcement, which may require addressing AI generated online content as a potential threat to school safety (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(4)).
  • If an institution's AI systems generate deepfake sexual imagery, that conduct may be classified as power based violence under the Campus Accountability and Safety Act, potentially triggering reporting and disciplinary obligations under that Part (R.S. 17:3399.12(5)(b)).

Notable exemptions

  • not stated in the text

Compliance steps

  • By fall semester 2026, develop information regarding power based violence, campus safety, internet and cell phone safety, and online content that is a potential threat to school safety, in consultation with campus or local law enforcement (R.S. 17:3399.16(A)).
  • Include instruction on identifying, preventing, dangers, and prohibition of power based violence, including AI or deepfake sexual imagery, and detecting potential threats online including social media (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(1)).
  • Include how to report incidents of power based violence, crimes, code violations, and threats (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(2)).
  • Include where to find campus safety reports (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(3)).
  • Update information in consultation with law enforcement (R.S. 17:3399.16(B)(4)).
  • Distribute information at least four times per academic year through in-person or online delivery (R.S. 17:3399.16(A)).
  • Distribute as part of new student orientation and post on easily accessible website page (R.S. 17:3399.16(C)(1)).
  • If student is minor, provide information to parent or legal guardian (R.S. 17:3399.16(C)(2)).
